name: Bisotun
description: Bisotun is a limestone cliff in western Iran, near Kermanshah, that Darius the Great covered with a carved scene and a long text around 520 BC. High above an old road linking Babylon and Ecbatana, the king stands with a bow, foot on a defeated rival, while bound captives line up beside him. The text appears in three ancient languages, and it later helped scholars decipher cuneiform.
